activity_context.topic_title: Sums of Finite Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation

feedback.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=\frac{2}{3}$ and $N=5.$ We need to figure out the value of ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=27{(\frac{2}{3})}^{n},
$$

and therefore, we can calculate the first term ${a}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =27{(\frac{2}{3})}^{1} \\  & =18\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=18,r=\frac{2}{3}$ and $N=5$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{5}27{(\frac{2}{3})}^{n} & =18\cdot \frac{(1-{(\frac{2}{3})}^{5})}{(1-\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =18\cdot \frac{(1-\frac{32}{243})}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =18\cdot \frac{(\frac{211}{243})}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =\frac{422}{9}\end{aligned}
$$
